name: Newcastle upon Tyne

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers privately rented homes in Byker Old Town and the Greater High Cross area of Benwell, under a new designation that started on 1 October 2026 and runs to September 2031.
licensing.additional: Additional HMO licensing applies to smaller HMOs (three or more people from two or more households sharing amenities) in the areas designated by Cabinet in October 2024 for five years; larger HMOs need the national mandatory licence everywhere. Check an address on the council's licensing map.

housing: Newcastle's private rented sector is concentrated in Jesmond, Sandyford, Heaton and Fenham, where Victorian terraces and the two-storey Tyneside flats are let to students of Newcastle and Northumbria universities and to young professionals. The city centre has added purpose-built student blocks and Quayside apartments, while the west end and Byker have older terraces under selective licensing. Smaller HMOs in designated areas need an additional licence.
checkinTips: Tyneside flats in Heaton, Jesmond and Fenham: record which yard, bins and outhouse belong to the flat, and photograph the separate front door and stairs.
Student houses in Jesmond and Sandyford: photograph every bedroom lock, fire doors, smoke and heat alarms, and the shared kitchen.
Victorian terraces in Benwell, Elswick and Byker: photograph the back lane, yard gate, gutters and any damp on rear walls.
City-centre and Quayside apartments: note fob, key and post-box counts, and photograph balconies and window seals.
Licensed homes: photograph the selective or HMO licence and check it shows the right address and expiry date.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or safety concerns can contact Newcastle City Council's private sector housing team, which runs the licensing schemes and can inspect homes.
